title: Arkret Cross-Signing Reset
description: Payload content for ak.cross_signing.reset (schema_id ak.schema.cross_signing_reset.v1). High-risk operation that retires the current (SSK, USK) generation and requires one of four kinds of proof — see device-lifecycle.md §14. A successor ak.cross_signing.publish MUST follow within 24h.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier. Enters every proof's canonical transcript so the same proof bytes cannot be replayed from deployment A into deployment B (different trust_domain → different transcript → signature verification fails as invalid_signature). Receivers MUST check this matches their own trust_domain before doing any signature work, returning cross_domain_replay_rejected otherwise. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.1 and zh/identity/identity-did.md §3.6.

reset_event_id.description: Typed event_id of the Event Envelope carrying this reset payload. MUST equal the enclosing Event.event_id. Binding it into proof transcript prevents wrapping the same proof bytes into a different Event shell. Mismatch MUST be rejected as reset_event_id_mismatch.

previous_generation.description: The generation being retired; MUST equal the currently accepted publish generation.

new_generation.description: Generation that the successor ak.cross_signing.publish will use; MUST equal previous_generation + 1.

revoked_device_ids.description: Devices known compromised or lost. Reducer atomically revokes them and requires MLS leaf removal/rekey. Required for compromise and device_loss resets.

did_url.description: DID URL with required key fragment. Fragment characters constrained to the ASCII set `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]` (a strict subset of RFC 3986 unreserved, excluding `~`, plus `:`) for stable byte-comparable key ids; see the Arkret verification-method DID URL profile in identity/did-usage-and-verification.md section 2.2. DID method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0.

principal_signing_proof.description: Principal-control-key proof. The schema only encodes wire shape; key-class verification is normative in zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4. `verification_method` MUST be a principal-grade DID-control verification method (zh/identity/key-management.md §3.2 — e.g. `did:webvh:...#ak_principal_signing_v1` or the DID method's equivalent control key), and MUST NOT be the self_signing_key or user_signing_key being retired by this reset.

verification_method.description: Principal-grade control-key verification method. MUST NOT reference the SSK/USK being reset (§14.4 rule (a)).

recovery_unlock_proof.description: Recovery-key unlock proof. The cryptographic strength comes entirely from `signature` — possession of the recovery private key is proven by verifying `signature` over the §14.1 canonical input under the public key bound to `recovery_secret_ref` in the recovery session's snapshotted accepted recovery_policy. A DID Document-only recovery key is not authoritative. `unlock_commitment` is a wire-integrity / debug binding only: it is a deterministic public hash that the receiver re-computes from material already in the event. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4: (a) recovery_secret_ref MUST resolve to a recovery_keys[] entry that was authoritative at issued_at; (b) signature MUST verify against that entry's public key; (c) unlock_commitment MUST equal SHA-256(utf8('ak.cross-signing-reset-unlock-binding-v1\n') || recovery_secret_ref || unlock_binding_input_bytes), where unlock_binding_input_bytes is the §14.1 canonical input with proof_body excluding both signature fields and unlock_commitment. Receivers MUST reject the reset if any of (a)-(c) fails.

recovery_session_id.description: Recovery session id from the §15 device recovery state machine (step 2). Carried inside the recovery_unlock proof body so it enters the §14.1 canonical transcript via proof_body, giving the proof a self-contained freshness binding that does not depend on external recovery state. Receivers MUST reject a recovery_unlock reset whose recovery_session_id does not match an active recovery session for principal_id at issued_at. See zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.1 / §15.

recovery_secret_ref.description: Stable verification_method identifier of a recovery_keys[] signing entry inside the recovery session's snapshotted accepted recovery_policy (e.g. `did:webvh:...#recovery-proof-1`). MUST match an entry that was authoritative, unexpired and unrevoked at issued_at; a DID Document-only key or recovery share id is invalid.

unlock_commitment.description: Deterministic wire-integrity hash bound to (recovery_secret_ref, reset content). Receiver-computable from public material; does NOT prove possession of the recovery secret — `signature` does. See §14.4 rule (c) for the exact derivation and the self-reference exclusion.

device_quorum_proof.description: Device-quorum proof. The schema enforces only the minimum wire shape (threshold>=2, signatures.minItems=1). Cryptographic and quorum verification are normative in zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §14.4: (a) every signature MUST verify against the public key of an authorized, non-revoked device in the principal's current device set at issued_at, over the §14.1 canonical input; (b) signatures MUST be deduplicated by device_id; (c) the count of valid, deduplicated signatures MUST be >= threshold; (d) threshold MUST equal the current `recovery_policy.device_quorum.k` (or equivalent published quorum policy) at issued_at — a smaller threshold supplied by the issuer MUST be rejected as `failed_precondition` reason=`cross_signing_reset_quorum_below_policy`. Receivers MUST reject the reset if any of (a)-(d) fails.

threshold.description: The quorum threshold the issuer claims to satisfy. MUST equal the principal's currently published recovery_policy device-quorum k (recovery_policy.device_quorum.k); receivers MUST cross-check (see description rule (d)).

signatures.description: minItems=1 is the schema floor only; reducer-side verification requires deduplicated valid signatures count >= threshold per description rule (c).

recovery_session_id.description: Verified, unexpired, unconsumed recovery session authenticated by principal_signing, recovery_unlock or device_quorum. A service-only session is not a second factor.

attestation_ref.description: Optional attestation object for service_id. If present, receivers MUST resolve it in the same trust_domain as the reset payload and reject cross-domain attestations as cross_signing_reset_recovery_service_attestation_domain_mismatch.
